summary.oneLiner: Pan-India provider of manpower services (manned security, IFM, sourcing/payroll), toll plaza management and skill development training, operating across 23 states and 5 union territories.
summary.business: Innovision provides manpower services (manned private security, integrated facility management, and manpower sourcing/payroll), toll plaza user-fee collection management, and government-scheme skill development training. It began with manned private security in 2007, added skill development in Fiscal 2014 and toll plaza management in Fiscal 2019. Through subsidiaries it also offers recruitment/visa facilitation (Innovision International) and remote-pilot drone training (Aerodrone Robotics).

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Pan-India provider of manpower services (manned security, IFM, sourcing/payroll), toll plaza management and skill development training, operating across 23 states and 5 union territories.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Established in 2007 and described as having "evolved from a manpower and security services company into a diversified infrastructure services platform with capabilities across toll plaza management, skill development and technology-enabled solutions", operating across 23 states and 5 Union Territories.
- "GOVERNMENT REVENUE CERTAINTY — 80%+ revenue linked to government ecosystem", with revenue exposure across NHAI, NSDC, MSDE and state government schemes and "sovereign-grade counterparties" said to support receivable quality; toll plaza management is stated as "100% sovereign counterparties".
- Claimed moat in toll: "NHAI VENDOR LOCK-IN — ₹5,759 Mn toll revenue in FY26 · Technical pre qualification, BG requirements, and 6-12-month approval cycles create high entry barriers".
- Manpower moat framed as "PSARA licensing & 14,000+ pan-India workforce" against an organised sector of only ~20-25% of the market, with formalisation (GST, PF, ESIC, labour codes) shifting share to listed players.
- "19-YEAR EXECUTION TRACK RECORD" and "Early mover in toll management and emerging Drone opportunities"; Aerodrone is claimed as a "First-mover listed drone platform in India" under the FY27-28 target state.

end_markets.body:

- Private clients across healthcare, retail, warehousing, logistics, BFSI

certifications.title: Certs (RHP)
certifications.body:
- PSARA (Private Security Agencies Regulation Act) licences
- Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) certification

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Service business - no manufacturing supply chain. Labour-intensive; deploys own and empanelled/contract personnel across client premises. Note: customer-concentration percentages above are of the Manpower Services segment only (the DRHP does not provide a group-wide top-customer table); toll revenue is authority/NHAI-contract driven.

customers.title: Oem (RHP)
customers.body:
- NHAI (toll collection empanelment)
- Sector skill councils and state skill missions (skill development)
- Canadian agency (RCIC certification via Innovision International)

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Toll plaza management scaled sharply (₹333.33 mn FY23 to ₹5,014.33 mn FY25) to become the largest segment
- Government vs private client mix in manpower services
- Contract/tender win-rate and performance-guarantee obligations
- Working-capital cycle from receivables on government contracts

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body:
- FY26 was the listing year on BSE (code 544732) and NSE; net worth rose to ₹294.20 Cr in FY26 from ₹81.88 Cr in FY25, with reserves at ₹270.39 Cr versus ₹62.98 Cr.
- IPO proceeds are allocated to ₹51 Cr of debt repayment and ₹119 Cr of working capital across manpower and toll management.
- Working-capital leverage claim: "Every ₹10 Cr toll WC capable of unlocking ~₹120 Cr annual toll revenue", with toll bidding requiring a security deposit plus bank guarantee of 30 days of collection per plaza.
- Balance sheet mix shifted toward current borrowings of ₹119.82 Cr in FY26 (₹73.14 Cr in FY25) alongside non-current borrowings of ₹3.82 Cr (₹5.91 Cr); trade receivables ₹158.16 Cr versus ₹106.81 Cr, cash & equivalents ₹50.66 Cr and bank balances ₹168.51 Cr.
- The deck states no dividend policy or payout intention.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: Growth is service/contract-led rather than plant-led: expansion of manpower client base (180+ clients, 1,000+ premises), additional toll plaza tenders with NHAI/authorities, and new verticals in drone training and international recruitment/visa services.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- Wide geographical reach across 23 states and 5 union territories
- Diverse portfolio of manpower services enabling cross-sell and recurring business
- Established systems and processes supporting a scalable business model
- Experienced management and operational team
- Recruitment capability, domain knowledge and knowledge of labour regulations

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Gujarat Gas debarment (revoked on ₹2.07 mn payment) and NHAI contract termination + one-year debarment (challenged in Punjab & Haryana High Court) can bar participation in future tenders
- Top 10 manpower clients ~57% of segment revenue; toll plaza segment 56% of total revenue dependent on tender renewals
- Revenue tied to competitive tenders, earnest-money deposits and performance guarantees
- Labour-intensive service model with receivables from government/PSU clients
- Licensing and statutory labour compliance across many states

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Repay/prepay borrowings from net proceeds**
- **Fund incremental working capital requirements from net proceeds**
- **Expand pan-India operations across states/UTs and client premises**
- **Build drone-operations / remote-pilot training through Aerodrone Robotics**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Deepen relationships with existing clients to capture greater share of their manpower requirements
- Expand toll plaza management footprint via NHAI/authority tenders
- Grow skill development as training partner for central/state government schemes
- Develop drone-operations training through Aerodrone Robotics subsidiary

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Milestone dating] The milestone timeline is internally inconsistent: the year row 2007/2014/2019/2020/2024/2025/2025/2025/2026/2027 is paired with events including "Crossed ₹500 Cr consolidated turnover milestone" appearing before "Crossed ₹200 Cr consolidated turnover milestone", so individual year-to-event bindings should not be relied on.
- [Leadership] Promoter, Chairman & MD is Lt Col Randeep Hundal, an Indian Army officer with 15+ years in manpower, security training and IFM; CEO & Whole-Time Director is Uday Pal Singh with 15+ years in manpower solutions.
- [Market sizing cited] Addressable markets quoted from the deck: India Security, Manpower & IFM Market USD 937 Mn; NHAI Toll Collection Ecosystem USD 10 Bn (FY26 toll revenue, +14% YoY); PM Vishwakarma scheme outlay USD 1.56 Bn (FY24-FY28); Global AI in Video Surveillance USD 12.46 Bn by 2030; India Drone Market ₹9,000 Cr+ by 2030; Global DAAS TAM ₹900 Bn+ by 2030; Gov PLI Scheme for Drones ₹120 Cr+.
- [Chart binding lost] The share-price slide lists a shareholding legend ("Promoter & Promoter Group, FIIs, DIIs, Public") with no percentages surviving extraction, and the price/volume chart carries no readable series values, so no shareholding split is asserted.
- [Recognitions] CAPSI "Best Man Guarding Company of the Year – 2024", ASSOCHAM training-programme awards (2017, 2018, 2019) and Indian Achievers' Forum "Brand Impact Award – 2022"; certifications listed as ISO 9001:2008, ISO/IEC 27001:2005, ISO 14001:2015 and OHSAS 18001:2007.
